cohort: The study included 2028 birthing persons and 2327 newborns delivered from 22-24 completed weeks gestation at 13 US centers between 2011-2020.
finding: Intervention rates for extremely early newborns increased and intercenter variability changed over time, with attempted resuscitation significantly associated with increasing gestational age and birth weight, Black birthing person race, previous premature delivery, and delivery center.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery at 23 weeks gestation significantly increased from 28.0% in epoch 1 to 44.7% in epoch 2.
birth_weight: N/A (birth weight was a factor associated with outcomes, but a specific range for the cohort was not mentioned)
